scenarios.title: Recover staged edits without ownership or capacity leaks
plannedActions: Finish the original 29 requests, add one synthetic auth session for the existing member, and capture the five-item two-event baseline through viewer reads.

Prepare a first-session scene draft beside the original invalid-part draft. Refuse a second-session draft at per-user capacity; refuse correct-byte uploads from another user and another auth session, then accept the original-session upload.

Refuse a different-user takeover prepare. Refuse same-user/different-auth-session prepare and confirm the original draft no longer accepts parts. Prepare the second-session draft and refuse a third capacity probe.

Upload and commit the second-session scene. Validate exact receipt, authored snapshot addition and one snapshotRequired event. Recover its receipt from the first session; refuse changed-user/label replay and verify unchanged public state.
Re-stage the original missing-reference batch and upload it. Refuse a third capacity probe, then refuse its invalid-reference commit and verify unchanged snapshot/events.
Re-prepare the discarded first-session draft. Require batch_incomplete before re-upload; a third probe remains refused. Re-upload and commit once, validating exact scene/event addition.

Recover both accepted receipts through the second session with no extra changes. Fill the other slot with a probe, refuse a third draft, and reuse the original invalid-part manifest at capacity; invalid part and missing-part commit remain refused.
Preserve all original users/sessions plus exactly the added fixture session, five original document items and old events, empty R2, 74 HTTP checks and zero outbound.
expectedOutcomes: The original invalid-part draft and a new first-session draft occupy both per-user slots. Preparing a second draft from another valid auth session of that same user returns exact 429/batch_capacity. Five quota refusals, interleaved with successful prepares/commits and cleanup, distinguish freed capacity from accidentally dropping unrelated staging. At the end a probe fills the other slot, a third draft is refused, and the original invalid-part manifest remains reusable at capacity but cannot commit without valid parts. No room-wide byte/count or expiry limit is tested.

An authorized different user and a second auth session of the same user cannot upload the first-session draft: both return exact 409/batch_session_changed. Original-session upload still succeeds. A different-user prepare returns command_reused without allowing takeover; same-user/different-auth-session prepare returns batch_session_changed and the old upload then reports batch_incomplete. Re-preparing that discarded draft later cannot commit until its part is uploaded again. Internal staging rows are not read.

Two valid new scene batches commit once each, producing exact snapshotRequired receipts and events at sequences three and four, with unchanged epoch/timing and all five original items preserved. An invalid-reference commit leaves nonlease snapshot/history unchanged and frees capacity for the next draft. Three exact accepted-receipt recoveries across the same user auth sessions return their original receipts without new document/event changes; different-user or changed-label replay returns command_reused. Users and all seeded session rows remain exact, R2 empty and outbound zero.

associations.rationale: Session mismatch and semantic commit failure use targeted draft/part disposal. Public missing-part and capacity probes distinguish cleanup from stale uploaded-part resurrection; no raw table proof.
associations.uncertainty: Independent review required. Sequential public HTTP and synthetic auth session; no internal staging/receipt reads, forced race/fault, TTL/alarm, room maximum, permission transition, restart/crash, live provider or native guarantee. Mapping is not measured execution.
proposedAssertions: After a cross-auth-session prepare refuses the first staged edit, its original-session upload is batch_incomplete. Re-preparing later yields batch_incomplete on commit until the same part is uploaded again, after which the scene commits once. This observes manifest/part disposal through public routes, not direct storage-row inspection.
